readings.text: 1 In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. 2 Now the earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.

3 And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light. 4 God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness. 5 God called the light "day," and the darkness he called "night." And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.
God makes the sky, the land and seas, plants and trees, the sun, moon and stars, the fish and birds, and all the animals. Each time, God saw that it was good.

26 Then God said, "Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground."
27 So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.

28 God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living creature that moves on the ground."

29 Then God said, "I give you every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole earth and every tree that has fruit with seed in it. They will be yours for food. 30 And to all the beasts of the earth and all the birds in the sky and all the creatures that move along the ground—everything that has the breath of life in it—I give every green plant for food." And it was so.
31 God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.

story: Long, long ago, before there were any people, animals, trees or even a sun, there was God. God has always been there. Everything else was dark and empty.
Then God spoke: "Let there be light!" And light appeared, just because God said so. He called the light "day" and the dark "night." That was the very first day.

God kept creating. He spread out the big blue sky. He gathered the water into seas and made dry land appear. He filled the land with plants, flowers and fruit trees. He put the bright sun in the sky for daytime and the moon and stars for nighttime. He filled the oceans with fish and giant sea creatures, and he filled the sky with birds. Then he made every kind of animal: puppies and horses, lions and bugs. Every time, God looked at what he made and saw that it was good.

Then God made something extra special: people. He made them in his own image, which means people are made to be like God in special ways. We can love, think, create, talk with God and take care of his world. God blessed the people and gave them a job: take care of everything he made.
At the end of the sixth day, God looked at everything and said it was very good.
weeks.enochLine: God made everything, and God made me!
enochActivities: Activity: "God Made It!" pointing game. Walk around the house or yard. Point at things God made (the sky, a tree, a dog, Mommy, Daddy, Jordyn, Elijah, Enoch!) and say together, "God made it!"
Paw Patrol touch: the pups have a job helping Adventure Bay, and God gave people a job too, taking care of his world. For extra fun, have Enoch draw his favorite animal God made.
elijahQuestions: What was the very first thing God made after he spoke?
After God made each thing, what did he say about it? What did he say after he made people?
God made a huge number of different animals. Which one do you think is the coolest, and what does it show you about how creative God is?
God made people "in his image." What is one way you can be like God this week, maybe by being kind, telling the truth, or helping someone?
jordynQuestions: Verse 3 says God simply spoke and light appeared. What does that tell us about how powerful God is compared to anything else?
What do you think it means to be made "in the image of God"? How should that change the way we treat people, including people who are hard to get along with?
God gave people the job to "rule over" and care for creation. How is ruling God's way, like a good caretaker, different from just being in charge?
weeks.jordynApplication: Everyone you meet this week, on your volleyball team, at school, or at home, is made in God's image. Pick one person who might feel left out or overlooked and do something on purpose to show them they matter: an encouraging word, a high-five after a play, or sitting with them. Your worth comes from the God who made you on purpose and called it very good, not from how well you play or what others think.
elijahAnswers: After each part of creation he said it was good. After he made people he said it was very good (v. 31).
Any animal is fine. The point is God's creativity: variety, beauty, and design show how wise and imaginative he is.
Examples: being kind, telling the truth, helping at home, caring for a pet or creation. "In his image" means we can love, create, speak truth, and care for others the way God does.
jordynAnswers: God's word alone has power to create. Nothing else is that powerful; he is not limited by tools, time, or materials.

Being made in God's image means people have God-given dignity and worth. We should treat everyone with respect and kindness, even people who are hard to get along with, because they bear his image too.
God's kind of ruling is serving and caring for what he made, not bossing people around for selfish gain. Like a good shepherd or caretaker, not a bully.
weeks.applicationCheck: Look for one concrete person she can encourage this week (teammate, classmate, sibling) and celebrate that her worth comes from God, not performance.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you for making the whole world: the light, the sky, the oceans, the animals, and us. Thank you for making each person in our family in your image and on purpose. Help us remember that you made everything and that everything belongs to you. Help us take good care of your world and treat everyone with kindness, because they are made by you too. We love you. In Jesus' name, Amen.

readings.text: 16 As soon as Jesus was baptized, he went up out of the water. At that moment heaven was opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. 17 And a voice from heaven said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased."
Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

story: There is only one God. He is not one god among many. The Bible says, "The LORD our God, the LORD is one."

This one God is three persons: the Father, the Son (Jesus), and the Holy Spirit. Each one is fully God. The Father is God. Jesus is God. The Holy Spirit is God. They are not three gods, and they are not one person putting on three different masks.

We cannot fully understand this, because God is greater than we are. People sometimes invent pictures to try to explain it, like water that can be ice, liquid, or steam. Pictures like that always fall short. Ice, water, and steam are forms of the same thing, usually one at a time. But at Jesus' baptism, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit were all there at the same time, as distinct persons. So we do not lean on a picture. We trust what God has shown us.

At the Jordan River, Jesus was baptized. As soon as he came up out of the water, the Holy Spirit came down on him like a dove, and the Father's voice from heaven said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased." We meet all three persons at once.

Before Jesus returned to heaven, he told his followers to make disciples of all nations and baptize them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. That is one name, and three persons.
Paul later blessed the church with all three together: the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit.
weeks.enochLine: There is one God: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit!
enochActivities: Activity: "One and three" finger count. Hold up one finger and say, "One God!" Then hold up three fingers and say, "Father, Son, and Holy Spirit!" Then go back to one finger: "One God!"

Paw Patrol touch: you can make it a mission, like the pups heading out to help. Enoch's mission is to remember who God is. For extra fun, have him draw the baptism story: Jesus in the water, a dove, and a bright sky for the Father's voice. Tell him the picture helps us remember the story, but no picture can show everything about God.
elijahQuestions: What does Deuteronomy 6:4 say about the LORD our God?
At Jesus' baptism in Matthew 3:16–17, who was in the water? Who came down like a dove? Who spoke from heaven?
In Matthew 28:19, Jesus says to baptize people in the name of whom?
2 Corinthians 13:14 names Jesus, God, and the Holy Spirit together in one blessing. What does that show us about God?
jordynQuestions: At Jesus' baptism, all three persons appear at the same time, doing different things. What does that tell us about whether the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are just three names for one person?
Deuteronomy 6:4 says the LORD is one, and Matthew 28:19 speaks of "the name" of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. How do those words guard us from thinking there are three gods?
Why is it wiser to say what the Bible shows — one God, three persons — than to explain God with a picture like water, ice, and steam?
weeks.jordynApplication: This week, when you pray before a volleyball game, at school, or at home, speak to the one God as he has made himself known: thank the Father who loves you, trust Jesus the Son who came for you, and ask the Holy Spirit to help you. If a friend asks who Christians worship, you can say simply: we worship one God — the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
elijahAnswers: "The LORD our God, the LORD is one." (Deuteronomy 6:4)

Jesus had just been baptized and came up out of the water. The Spirit of God came down like a dove and rested on him. The Father spoke from heaven: "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased." (Matthew 3:16–17)
In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19).
It shows that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit belong together as the one God. This is one blessing from one God, not three separate gods.
jordynAnswers: They are distinct persons. At the same moment, the Son is baptized, the Spirit descends, and the Father speaks. That is not one person switching roles or names.
There is one God (Deuteronomy 6:4). Jesus speaks of one "name," then names the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. One name, three persons — not three gods.

Pictures like water, ice, and steam describe one thing taking different forms, often at different times. Other pictures fail in other ways. At Jesus' baptism the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are all present at once, each fully God, and still one God. Every picture falls short, so we stay with what Scripture shows and admit the mystery with humility.
weeks.applicationCheck: Listen for her naming Father, Son, and Holy Spirit as one God, and notice a specific prayer or conversation this week.
weeks.prayer: Dear God, thank you that you are the one true God. Thank you, Father, for loving us. Thank you, Jesus, for coming to us. Thank you, Holy Spirit, for being with us. We cannot understand everything about you, but we believe what you have shown us. Help our family love you, trust you, and tell the truth about who you are. We love you. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.focus: There is one God: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
dailies.verse: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
dailies.enoch: Hold up one finger and say, "One God!" Then hold up three fingers and say, "Father, Son, and Holy Spirit!"
dailies.elijah: In Matthew 28:19, Jesus says to baptize people in the name of whom?
dailies.jordyn: Why does Jesus say "the name" of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, not "the names"?
dailies.elijahAnswer: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19).
dailies.jordynAnswer: One "name" points to one God. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are three persons, not three gods.
dailies.action: Say Matthew 28:19 out loud together two times.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you that you are one God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Help us remember your name. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.focus: The LORD our God is one.
dailies.verse: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
dailies.enoch: Say with the family, "The LORD our God, the LORD is one!"
dailies.elijah: What does Deuteronomy 6:4 tell us about the LORD our God?
dailies.jordyn: Why does it matter that Christians worship one God, not three gods?
dailies.elijahAnswer: "The LORD our God, the LORD is one." (Deuteronomy 6:4)
dailies.jordynAnswer: There is only one God. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are not three gods; they are three persons who are the one God.
dailies.action: When you hear the word "God" today, quietly remember: there is only one God.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you that you are the one true God. Help us love you with our whole heart. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.focus: At Jesus' baptism we meet the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit at the same time.
dailies.verse: 16 As soon as Jesus was baptized, he went up out of the water. At that moment heaven was opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. 17 And a voice from heaven said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased."
dailies.enoch: Who was in the water? (Jesus!) Who came down like a dove? (the Holy Spirit!) Who spoke from heaven? (the Father!)
dailies.elijah: At Jesus' baptism, who was in the water, who came down like a dove, and who spoke from heaven?
dailies.jordyn: All three persons appear at the same time, doing different things. What does that tell us about whether they are just three names for one person?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Jesus was in the water. The Spirit of God came down like a dove. The Father spoke from heaven (Matthew 3:16–17).
dailies.jordynAnswer: They are distinct persons. At the same moment, the Son is baptized, the Spirit descends, and the Father speaks. That is not one person switching roles or names.
dailies.action: Act out the baptism scene in about 30 seconds: one person standing as Jesus, one showing the Spirit coming down like a dove, and one speaking the Father's words.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you that at Jesus' baptism we see you as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Help us trust what you have shown us. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.focus: The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit bless us together.
dailies.verse: May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
dailies.enoch: Repeat: "Thank you, Jesus. Thank you, Father. Thank you, Holy Spirit."
dailies.elijah: Which three names do you hear in this blessing?
dailies.jordyn: How does this one blessing show that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit belong together as one God?
dailies.elijahAnswer: The Lord Jesus Christ, God (the Father), and the Holy Spirit (2 Corinthians 13:14).
dailies.jordynAnswer: It is one blessing, not three separate blessings from three gods. The grace of Jesus, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit come together from the one God.
dailies.action: Read 2 Corinthians 13:14 out loud as a blessing over your family at dinner or bedtime.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you for the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.focus: Pray to the one God as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
dailies.verse: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
dailies.enoch: Say, "Thank you, Father. Thank you, Jesus. Thank you, Holy Spirit."
dailies.elijah: What is one thing you can thank God for today: something about the Father, about Jesus, or about the Holy Spirit?
dailies.jordyn: If a friend asked who Christians worship, what would you say in one sentence?
dailies.elijahAnswer: Any true answer is fine: thank the Father for loving us and making us, thank Jesus for coming to us, or thank the Holy Spirit for being with us.
dailies.jordynAnswer: We worship one God — the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
dailies.action: Pray once today naming the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, before school, practice, or bed.
dailies.prayer: Dear Father, thank you for loving us. Dear Jesus, thank you for coming to us. Dear Holy Spirit, thank you for being with us. In Jesus' name, Amen.

dailies.focus: One God, three persons, each fully God.
dailies.verse: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
dailies.enoch: Do the one-and-three finger count again: "One God!" then "Father, Son, and Holy Spirit!" then "One God!"
dailies.elijah: Are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit three gods, or one God?
dailies.jordyn: Why do pictures like water, ice, and steam fall short of describing God?
dailies.elijahAnswer: One God. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are three persons, each fully God, not three gods.
dailies.jordynAnswer: Pictures like water, ice, and steam describe one thing taking different forms, often at different times. At Jesus' baptism the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are all present at once, each fully God, and still one God. Every picture falls short, so we stay with what the Bible shows.
dailies.action: Recite Matthew 28:19 together, then play the finger-count game three times.
dailies.prayer: Dear God, thank you that you are the one true God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Help our family tell the truth about who you are. In Jesus' name, Amen.
